instructions:
Each item is an ontology term that a column of sample metadata in a gene
expression study can mean. Write up to 5 aliases for each term: other ways a
researcher would write that same variable as a column header in sample
metadata.

Good aliases:
- common abbreviations and acronyms ("sbp" for systolic blood pressure)
- shorter everyday phrasings ("systolic bp", "visual acuity")
- the plain name of the quantity when the term's label is wordy
  ("intraocular pressure" for "intraocular pressure measurement")

Rules:
- An alias must mean the same variable as the term: not a broader or narrower
  one, and not a related one.
- No values ("male", "high"), units on their own, gene or tool names, or
  dataset-specific codes.
- No alias that only rewords the label trivially (plural, case,
  punctuation). Those are matched already.
- Fewer is better than wrong. If a term has no natural alias, return an empty
  list.

Examples:
- systolic blood pressure -> ["sbp", "systolic bp", "systolic pressure"]
- intraocular pressure measurement -> ["intraocular pressure", "iop"]
- visual acuity measurement -> ["visual acuity", "va"]

items.label: hypertrophy
items.definition: Hypertrophy is the increase in the volume of an organ or tissue due to the enlargement of its component cells.

items.label: cardiac hypertrophy
items.definition: an increase in size of the cardiac tissue, not due to increased cell number

items.label: primary cell
items.definition: A cell taken directly from a living organism, which is not immortalized.

items.label: experimental process
items.definition: A process performed as part of an experiment or wider study, i.e. intentionally designed.

items.label: benign
items.definition: For neoplasms, a non-infiltrating and non-metastasizing neoplastic process that is characterized by the absence of morphologic features associated with malignancy (e.g., severe atypia, nuclear pleomorphism, tumor cell necrosis, and abnormal mitoses). items.label: nucleic acid extraction protocol
items.definition: A protocol description in which a material separation to recover the nucleic acid fraction of an input material is performed

items.label: parous
items.definition: The quality of an organism that has successful reproduced.

items.label: pregnancy
items.definition: The status during which female mammals carry their developing young (EMBRYOS or FETUSES) in utero before birth, beginning from FERTILIZATION to BIRTH.

items.label: virgin
items.definition: The quality of an organism that has never been sexually active.

items.label: differentiated
items.definition: A property of a cell which is no longer pluripotent

items.label: pluripotent
items.definition: A property of a cell which is able to differentiate into into one or more differentiated cell types

items.label: heart transplant rejection

items.label: sign or symptom
items.definition: Objective evidence of disease perceptible to the examining physician (sign) and subjective evidence of disease perceived by the patient (symptom).

items.label: gene expression protocol
items.definition: A gene expression protocol is a  protocol which is designed to be used in a gene expression experiment performed on arrays or by high throughput sequencing.

items.label: growth protocol
items.definition: A growth protocol is a protocol which provides instructions on the growth of a biological sample. E.g. the growth of a specific cell line or Drosophila culture

items.label: hybridization protocol
items.definition: A hybridization protocol is the set of instructions or plan for performing a nucleic acid hybridization on an microarray such as those provided by Affymetrix

items.label: labelling protocol
items.definition: A labelling protocol is a set of instructions or plan which is realised

items.label: sample treatment protocol
items.definition: A sample treatment protocol is a protocol used in a biological experiment and defines instructions on how a sample should be treated in a given experimental scenario.

items.label: nucleic acid labeling protocol
items.definition: A protocol description in which input nucleic acid material is labeled.

items.label: array scanning and feature extraction protocol
items.definition: A protocol describing an image acquisition process that generates an image and features extracted in numerical form from an array.

items.label: nucleic acid hybridization to array protocol
items.definition: A protocol describing the hybridisation of the target nucleic acid sample to a fixed probe on the array.

items.label: normalization data transformation protocol
items.definition: A protocol describing a data transformation in which data transformation has the objective normalization.

items.label: hyperemia
items.definition: The presence of an increased amount of blood in a part or organ; engorgement.

items.label: calcification
items.definition: Process by which organic tissue becomes hardened by the physiologic deposit of calcium salts.

items.label: pulmonary function measurement
items.definition: Measurement of the various processes involved in the act of respiration: inspiration, expiration, oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange, lung volume and compliance, etc.

items.label: dysuria
items.definition: Painful URINATION. It is often associated with infections of the lower URINARY TRACT.

items.label: premature birth
items.definition: CHILDBIRTH before 37 weeks of PREGNANCY (259 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period, or 245 days after FERTILIZATION).

items.label: risk factor
items.definition: Any aspect of an individual's life, behavior, an environmental exposure, or an inborn or inherited characteristic that increases the likelihood of a disease, condition or injury.

items.label: hair color
items.definition: Color of hair or fur.

items.label: cognition
items.definition: Intellectual or mental process whereby an organism becomes aware of or obtains knowledge.

items.label: menarche
items.definition: The first MENSTRUAL CYCLE marked by the initiation of MENSTRUATION.

items.label: mental health
items.definition: The state wherein the person is well adjusted.

items.label: energy intake
items.definition: Total number of calories taken in daily whether ingested or by parenteral routes.

items.label: physical activity
items.definition: The physical activity of a human or an animal as a behavioral phenomenon.

items.label: personality
items.definition: Behavior-response patterns that characterize the individual.

items.label: eye color
items.definition: Color of the iris.

items.label: fever of unknown origin
items.definition: Fever in which the etiology cannot be ascertained.

items.label: hormone replacement therapy
items.definition: Therapeutic use of hormones to alleviate the effects of hormone deficiency.

items.label: treatment protocol
items.definition: A protocol in which the aim is to treat a sample, collection of samples, organism or group of organisms for some experimental analysis of outcome.

items.label: duplication
items.definition: A genetic modification in which part of the genome is duplicated

items.label: spontaneous mutation
items.definition: A genetic modification which has arisen by a spontaneous mutation in an individual.

items.label: targeted mutation
items.definition: A genetic modification in which a targeted mutation has been introduced into the genome of an individual

items.label: transgenic
items.definition: A genetic modification in which a transgene has been inserted into an individual

items.label: transposition
items.definition: A genetic modification introduced into an individual as the result of transposase activity

items.label: translocation
items.definition: A type of chromosome rearrangement in which two nonhomologous chromosomes are each broken and then repaired

items.label: gene trap

items.label: scanned image
items.definition: An image prodcued as the result of a scan, such as a medical scanner or array scanner.

items.label: data file
items.definition: A file stored for use on a computer containing data.

items.label: processed array data file
items.definition: A data file containing array data which has been processed in some way using a data transformation.

items.label: MAGE-TAB array data matrix file
items.definition: An array data file which has been transformed into a matrix format as defined by MAGE-TAB specification.

items.label: array data file
items.definition: A data file which contains data produced as the result of running an array.

items.label: tumor size
items.definition: The physical size of a tumor.

items.label: Sequence Read Format (SRF)
items.definition: Sequence Read file forma is a generic format for DNA sequence data capable of storing data generated by any DNA sequencing technology.

items.label: FASTQ format
items.definition: FASTQ format is a text-based format for storing both a biological sequence (usually nucleotide sequence) and its corresponding quality scores.

items.label: Standard Flowgram Format (SFF)
items.definition: Standard flowgram format (SFF) is a binary file format used to encode results of pyrosequencing from the 454 Life Sciences platform for high-throughput sequencing.

items.label: BAM format
items.definition: BAM is the compressed binary version of the Sequence Alignment/Map (SAM) format

items.label: nucleic acid sequencing protocol
items.definition: A protocol describing the processes performed and equipment used to determine the order of nucleotide bases in a nucleic acid sample

items.label: cot filtration for single or low copy genomic DNA
items.definition: A type of cot filtration in which single/low copy sequences and the repetitive sequences of a genome to be studied independently of each other.

items.label: cot filtration for moderately repetitive genomic DNA
items.definition: A type of cot filtration in which moderately repetitive sequences and highly repetitive sequences of a genome can be separated to be studied independently of each other.

items.label: cot filtration for highly repetitive genomic DNA
cot filtration for theoretical single copy genomic DNA
nucleic acid library construction protocol
items.definition: A protocol describing the processes performed and equipment used to prepare nucleic acid sequencing library.

items.label: vaccination
items.definition: A process that involves adding vaccine into a host (e.g., human, mouse) in vivo with the intent to invoke a protective immune response.

items.label: recombination
items.definition: Production of new arrangements of DNA by various mechanisms such as assortment and segregation, CROSSING OVER; GENE CONVERSION; GENETIC TRANSFORMATION; GENETIC CONJUGATION; GENETIC TRANSDUCTION; or mixed infection of viruses.

items.label: left atrial function
items.definition: The hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the LEFT ATRIUM.

items.label: left ventricular function
items.definition: The hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the left HEART VENTRICLE. Its measurement is an important aspect of the clinical evaluation of patients with heart disease to determine the effects of the disease on cardiac performance.

items.label: thyroid function
items.definition: Physiological activity and functions of the highly vascular thyroid gland, such as producing the thyroid hormones which are concerned in regulating the metabolic rate of the body.

items.label: clinical laboratory measurement
items.definition: A clinical laboratory measurement is a measurement of some entity e.g. erythrocyte count or metabolite panel which is used in the process of clinical diagnosis in human patients

items.label: cardiovascular measurement
items.definition: A cardiovascular measurement is a measurement of some part of the cardiovascular system and is typically used  in the process of disease diagnosis in human patients.

items.label: life expectancy
items.definition: Based on known statistical data, the number of years which any person of a given age may reasonably be expected to live.

items.label: anthropometric measurement
items.definition: Anthropometry is a measurement of the size, weight, and proportions of the human or other primate body.

items.label: vital signs
items.definition: The signs of life that may be monitored or measured, namely pulse rate, respiratory rate, body temperature, and blood pressure.

items.label: erythrocyte count
items.definition: The number of red blood cells per unit volume in a sample of venous blood.

items.label: erythrocyte indices
items.definition: ERYTHROCYTE size and HEMOGLOBIN content or concentration, usually derived from ERYTHROCYTE COUNT; BLOOD hemoglobin concentration; and HEMATOCRIT. The indices include the mean corpuscular volume (MCV), the mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH), and the mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC).

items.label: glucose tolerance test
items.definition: Quantification of the ability of an individual to maintain homeostasis of blood glucose, via a test procedure including measuring blood glucose levels in a fasting state, and at prescribed intervals before and after oral glucose intake (75 or 100 g) or intravenous infusion (0.5 g/kg).

items.label: platelet count
items.definition: The number of PLATELETS per unit volume in a sample of venous BLOOD.

items.label: vital capacity
items.definition: The volume of air that is exhaled by a maximal expiration following a maximal inspiration.
